chapter_text:
CHAPTER 3 — त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् (TYAJYAM NA DHAIRYAM)

Introduction — त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् कथयति किम्?

The title of this lesson, त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् (tyajyam na dhairyam), means "Courage must never be abandoned." It is built from three words: त्याज्यम् (tyajyam), न (na) and धैर्यम् (dhairyam). धैर्यम् means firmness, patience and courage — the steadiness of mind that keeps a person calm and determined. न means "not". त्याज्यम् is a special verb-derived word called a कृत्य (gerundive), formed from the धातु (root) √त्यज् ("to abandon, to give up"); it means "that which is to be given up / ought to be given up". So त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् literally says: "Courage is NOT a thing to be given up." Whatever else a person may lose in life, courage and patience should never be lost.

Why courage and perseverance matter (धैर्यस्य महत्त्वम्)

Life brings both good days and bad days. Difficulties (आपद्), obstacles (विघ्न) and failures come to everyone. In such moments a weak person becomes a कातर (coward), loses heart and gives up; but a धीर (steadfast) person keeps a calm, courageous mind, thinks clearly, and keeps working towards the goal. Sanskrit poets and teachers understood this deeply, and composed many beautiful नीति-verses (subhashitas) praising steadiness of mind. These verses teach a simple but powerful truth: obstacles are temporary, but the one who does not abandon धैर्य finally succeeds. In this lesson we read four famous public-domain Sanskrit verses on courage and perseverance, learn their word meanings (शब्दार्थ), translate them into simple English, draw out their morals, and use them to learn a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Four verses on courage and perseverance (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
   प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ।
   विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
   प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति ॥
   शब्दार्थ: प्रारभ्यते = is begun; न = not; खलु = indeed; विघ्नभयेन = out of fear of obstacles; नीचैः = by the low (mean people); प्रारभ्य = having begun; विघ्नविहताः = struck/beaten by obstacles; विरमन्ति = stop, desist; मध्याः = the middling (average) people; विघ्नैः = by obstacles; पुनः पुनः = again and again; अपि = even; प्रतिहन्यमानाः = being repeatedly struck; प्रारब्धम् = the task begun; उत्तमजनाः = the noble (best) people; न परित्यजन्ति = do not abandon.
   Translation: Out of fear of obstacles, the low (नीच) never even begin a task. The middling (मध्यम), having begun, stop when obstacles strike them. But the noble (उत्तम), though struck again and again by obstacles, never abandon what they have begun.
   Theme / Moral: This is the great verse of perseverance. People are of three kinds — those who never start, those who quit midway, and those who never give up. True greatness lies in continuing to the very end. This verse is the heart of "त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्". (Bhartrhari, Nīti-śataka — public domain.)

2) आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा
   सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः ।
   यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ
   प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: आपदि = in adversity/calamity; धैर्यम् = courage; अथ = and; अभ्युदये = in prosperity; क्षमा = patience/forgiveness; सदसि = in the assembly; वाक्पटुता = eloquence (skill in speech); युधि = in battle; विक्रमः = valour; यशसि = in fame; अभिरुचिः = eagerness, liking; व्यसनम् = deep devotion; श्रुतौ = in learning/scripture; प्रकृतिसिद्धम् = natural, inborn; हि = indeed; महात्मनाम् = of great souls.
   Translation: Courage in adversity, patience in prosperity, eloquence in the assembly, valour in battle, love of good fame, and deep devotion to learning — these are the inborn (natural) qualities of great souls.
   Theme / Moral: A great person shows the right virtue in every situation. The very first quality named is आपदि धैर्यम् — courage in the hour of difficulty. (Bhartrhari, Nīti-śataka — public domain.)

3) उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम् ।
   सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उत्साहः = enthusiasm, zeal; बलवान् = powerful, mighty; आर्य = O noble one; न अस्ति = there is not; उत्साहात् = than enthusiasm; परम् = greater; बलम् = strength; सोत्साहस्य = of one full of enthusiasm; हि = indeed; लोकेषु = in the (three) worlds; न किञ्चित् अपि = nothing at all; दुर्लभम् = hard to attain.
   Translation: O noble one, enthusiasm is mighty; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For a person full of enthusiasm, nothing at all in the world is hard to attain.
   Theme / Moral: उत्साह (zeal and courage) is the greatest power. With enthusiasm and a steady mind, even the hardest goal becomes reachable. (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa — public domain.)

4) धैर्यं यस्य पिता क्षमा च जननी शान्तिः चिरं गेहिनी
   सत्यं सूनुरयं दया च भगिनी भ्राता मनःसंयमः ।
   शय्या भूमितलं दिशोऽपि वसनं ज्ञानामृतं भोजनं
   एते यस्य कुटुम्बिनो वद सखे कस्माद्भयं योगिनः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: धैर्यम् = courage; यस्य = whose; पिता = father; क्षमा = patience; जननी = mother; शान्तिः = peace; चिरम् = long, lifelong; गेहिनी = wife (of the house); सत्यम् = truth; सूनुः = son; अयम् = this; दया = compassion; भगिनी = sister; भ्राता = brother; मनःसंयमः = self-control (of the mind); शय्या = bed; भूमितलम् = the surface of the earth; दिशः = the directions (as) ; अपि = even; वसनम् = clothing; ज्ञानामृतम् = the nectar of knowledge; भोजनम् = food; एते = these; कुटुम्बिनः = family members; वद = tell (me); सखे = O friend; कस्मात् = from what; भयम् = fear; योगिनः = of the yogī.
   Translation: He whose father is courage, mother is patience, lifelong wife is peace, son is truth, sister is compassion, and brother is self-control; whose bed is the bare earth, whose clothing is the very directions, and whose food is the nectar of knowledge — tell me, friend, from what should such a yogī ever have fear?
   Theme / Moral: A life built on virtues — courage, patience, peace, truth, compassion, self-control — is fearless and content. Here धैर्य (courage) is honoured as the very "father" of the noble person. (Subhashita — public domain.)

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet in Sanskrit they often combine and change. Being able to SPLIT a joined form back into its parts (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill.
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि (long-vowel): a short vowel + a similar vowel merge into one long vowel. From verse 2: अथ + अभ्युदये → अथाभ्युदये (अ + अ = आ). From verse 4: ज्ञान + अमृतम् → ज्ञानामृतम् (अ + अ = आ). Also न + अस्ति → नास्ति in नास्त्युत्साहात् (verse 3).
  • यण्-सन्धि: इ/उ before a dissimilar vowel becomes य्/व्. In verse 3, अस्ति + उत्साहात् → अस्त्युत्साहात् (इ + उ → य् + उ), giving नास्त्युत्साहात्.
  • व्यञ्जन-सन्धि (जश्त्व): a hard त् before a soft sound becomes द्. In verse 4, कस्मात् + भयम् → कस्माद्भयम् (त् → द् before भ).
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि: in verse 4, दिशः + अपि → दिशोऽपि (visarga अः + अ → ओ, and the following अ is dropped, marked by the अवग्रह ऽ).

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role. Examples from the verses:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, the subject): धैर्यम्, क्षमा, उत्साहः — the doers/subjects.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): विघ्नैः "by obstacles" (plural), विघ्नभयेन "by fear of obstacles".
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, "than/from"): उत्साहात् "than enthusiasm".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): महात्मनाम् "of great souls" (plural), सोत्साहस्य "of the enthusiastic one", योगिनः "of the yogī".
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at"): आपदि "in adversity", अभ्युदये "in prosperity", सदसि "in the assembly", युधि "in battle", श्रुतौ "in learning", लोकेषु "in the worlds" (plural).

(C) धातुरूप (verb conjugation — worked example). The title word त्याज्यम् and the verb परित्यजन्ति (verse 1) both come from the धातु √त्यज् ("to abandon"). Its present-tense (लट्, परस्मैपद) forms are:
  • प्रथमपुरुष (3rd person): एकवचन त्यजति (he abandons), द्विवचन त्यजतः, बहुवचन त्यजन्ति (they abandon).
  • मध्यमपुरुष (2nd person): त्यजसि, त्यजथः, त्यजथ.
  • उत्तमपुरुष (1st person): त्यजामि (I abandon), त्यजावः, त्यजामः.
Notice that परित्यजन्ति in the verse is प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन ("they abandon"), with the prefix परि-; न परित्यजन्ति = "they do not abandon".

(D) शब्दरूप (noun declension — a note). Masculine a-stem nouns like नर decline in the प्रथमा (nominative) as: एकवचन नरः, द्विवचन नरौ, बहुवचन नराः. In the verses उत्साहः (verse 3) is such a प्रथमा एकवचन subject, while वृक्ष-type plurals take -आः.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् means "courage must never be abandoned" — from त्याज्यम् (a gerundive of √त्यज्, "to be given up") + न + धैर्यम्. You saw why steadiness of mind matters: difficulties come to everyone, and the one who keeps courage (धीर) succeeds while the coward (कातर) gives up. You read four famous public-domain verses — the perseverance verse प्रारभ्यते न खलु... (the noble never abandon a task), आपदि धैर्यम्... (great souls show the right virtue in every situation), उत्साहो बलवान्... (enthusiasm is the greatest strength), and धैर्यं यस्य पिता... (a life of virtues is fearless). For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, a translation and the moral. Finally you drew grammar from the verses: दीर्घ-, यण्-, व्यञ्जन- and विसर्ग-सन्धि (with सन्धि-विच्छेद), the common विभक्ति case-endings, and the present-tense धातुरूप of √त्यज्. Memorise these verses — त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् — and let courage be the one thing you never give up.

topics.name: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् — Meaning and the Value of Courage
topics.description: What त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् ('courage must never be abandoned') means, how त्याज्यम् is a gerundive of √त्यज्, and why steadiness of mind (धैर्य) matters in adversity — the difference between the धीर (steadfast) and the कातर (coward).

topics.name: Selected Verses on Courage and Perseverance
topics.description: Four famous public-domain Sanskrit verses on courage and perseverance — प्रारभ्यते न खलु..., आपदि धैर्यम्..., उत्साहो बलवान्..., and धैर्यं यस्य पिता... — presented with verse, meaning and context, and how to read and recite them.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary through word-by-word शब्दार्थ of each verse: words such as धैर्यम्, आपद्, अभ्युदय, क्षमा, विक्रम, उत्साह, विघ्न, दुर्लभम्, महात्मन् and their English meanings.

topics.name: Moral and Ethical Themes
topics.description: The moral and ethical themes carried by the verses — perseverance despite obstacles, courage in adversity, patience in prosperity, the power of enthusiasm, and fearlessness born of a life of virtues.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi, Vibhakti, Dhaturupa)
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the verses: दीर्घ, यण्, व्यञ्जन and विसर्ग सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद; the common विभक्ति case endings (प्रथमा to सप्तमी) with examples; and the present-tense धातुरूप of √त्यज्.

topics.name: Translation and Comprehension
topics.description: Translating the verses into simple English and answering comprehension questions — identifying the subject, case, key word meanings and the moral of a given verse on courage and perseverance.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् — Meaning and the Value of Courage
learning_outcomes.description: Explain what त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् means (त्याज्यम् + न + धैर्यम्) and describe why courage and perseverance must never be abandoned, even in adversity.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Selected Verses on Courage and Perseverance
learning_outcomes.description: Recall and recite the selected verses on courage and perseverance and identify each verse by its opening words and central idea.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: Selected Verses on Courage and Perseverance
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of a given verse as a whole and relate its imagery (three types of people, virtues as family, enthusiasm as strength) to its message.
Give the शब्दार्थ (word meaning) in English of Sanskrit words drawn from the verses and use the vocabulary of courage and perseverance correctly.
Analyse the moral or ethical theme of a verse on courage or perseverance and apply its lesson to everyday situations such as failure or difficulty.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi, Vibhakti, Dhaturupa)
learning_outcomes.description: Identify and perform simple सन्धि joins and splits (सन्धि-विच्छेद) — दीर्घ, यण्, व्यञ्जन and विसर्ग — using examples taken from the verses.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (Sandhi, Vibhakti, Dhaturupa)
learning_outcomes.description: Recognise the common विभक्ति case endings and the present-tense धातुरूप of √त्यज्, and state the case, person or number of a word in a verse.
Translate a given verse on courage or perseverance into simple English and answer comprehension questions about its words, grammar and moral.

chapter_summary.title: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् (Tyajyam na Dhairyam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 3. It explains that त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् means 'courage must never be abandoned', presents four famous public-domain verses on courage and perseverance with their meanings and morals, and draws simple grammar — सन्धि, विभक्ति and धातुरूप — from the verses.

branches.label: अर्थः — Meaning & Value
details: त्याज्यम् + न + धैर्यम् = courage not to be given up

branches.label: मूल्यानि — Themes/Morals
details: A life of virtues is fearless

sections.heading: What 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' means and why it matters
bullets: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् = 'courage must never be abandoned'; त्याज्यम् is a gerundive (कृत्य) of √त्यज् ('to give up'), न = not, धैर्यम् = courage/steadiness.
Difficulties (आपद्) and obstacles (विघ्न) come to everyone; the steadfast (धीर) keep courage while the coward (कातर) gives up.
Obstacles are temporary, but the one who does not abandon धैर्य finally succeeds — this is the theme of the whole chapter.

sections.heading: The perseverance verse (प्रारभ्यते न खलु...)
bullets: People are of three kinds: the low (नीच) never begin, for fear of obstacles.
The middling (मध्यम) begin but stop when obstacles strike.
The noble (उत्तम), though struck again and again, never abandon what they have begun (न परित्यजन्ति).
Moral: true greatness is to persevere to the very end.

sections.heading: Courage, patience and enthusiasm (आपदि धैर्यम्... / उत्साहो बलवान्...)
bullets: आपदि धैर्यम् — courage in adversity; अभ्युदये क्षमा — patience in prosperity; युधि विक्रमः — valour in battle.
These virtues are प्रकृतिसिद्ध — natural and inborn — in great souls (महात्मन्).
उत्साहो बलवान् — enthusiasm is mighty; नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम् — no strength is greater than zeal.
For the enthusiastic person, nothing in the world is दुर्लभ (hard to attain).

sections.heading: A life of virtues is fearless (धैर्यं यस्य पिता...)
bullets: The yogī's 'family' is made of virtues: courage as father, patience as mother, peace as wife, truth as son, compassion as sister, self-control as brother.
His bed is the earth, his clothing the directions, his food the nectar of knowledge (ज्ञानामृत).
With such a family of virtues, he has nothing to fear (कस्माद्भयं योगिनः).
Moral: a life built on good qualities is content and fearless.

sections.heading: Grammar from the verses (सन्धि, विभक्ति, धातुरूप)
bullets: दीर्घ-सन्धि: अथ + अभ्युदये = अथाभ्युदये; ज्ञान + अमृतम् = ज्ञानामृतम् (अ + अ = आ).
यण्-सन्धि: अस्ति + उत्साहात् = अस्त्युत्साहात् (इ + उ → य्); व्यञ्जन: कस्मात् + भयम् = कस्माद्भयम्; विसर्ग: दिशः + अपि = दिशोऽपि.
विभक्ति: सप्तमी आपदि/अभ्युदये/लोकेषु ('in'); तृतीया विघ्नैः ('by'); षष्ठी महात्मनाम् ('of').
धातुरूप of √त्यज् (लट्): त्यजति, त्यजतः, त्यजन्ति; परित्यजन्ति = 'they abandon' (3rd person plural).

key_takeaways: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् means 'courage must never be abandoned' — त्याज्यम् (gerundive of √त्यज्) + न + धैर्यम्.
The noble never give up a task despite repeated obstacles — प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति.
Keep courage in adversity and patience in prosperity — आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा.
Enthusiasm is the greatest strength; for the zealous nothing is unattainable — नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्.
A life built on virtues (courage, patience, peace, truth, compassion, self-control) is fearless.
सन्धि joins sounds (अथ + अभ्युदये = अथाभ्युदये); सन्धि-विच्छेद splits them back.
विभक्ति endings show a word's role: सप्तमी 'in', तृतीया 'by', षष्ठी 'of'; and √त्यज् gives त्यजति/त्यजतः/त्यजन्ति.

glossary.definition: Courage, firmness, patience — the steadiness of mind that must never be abandoned (न त्याज्यम्).
'That which is to be given up' — a gerundive (कृत्य) formed from the root √त्यज् ('to abandon').
The Sanskrit verb-root meaning 'to abandon / give up'; present forms त्यजति, त्यजतः, त्यजन्ति.
Calamity, adversity, misfortune; the situation in which one must keep धैर्य (आपदि धैर्यम्).
Prosperity, rise, success; the situation in which the wise show क्षमा (patience/forgiveness).
Patience, forbearance, forgiveness; praised as the proper virtue in times of prosperity.
Valour, prowess, heroism; the virtue great souls show in battle (युधि विक्रमः).
Enthusiasm, zeal, energy; called the greatest strength (नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्).
An obstacle or hindrance; the noble persevere though struck again and again by विघ्न.
The noble or best people, who never abandon a task they have begun (न परित्यजन्ति).
A great soul; one in whom courage, patience and valour are naturally (प्रकृतिसिद्ध) present.
A self-disciplined, virtuous person; in verse 4 one whose 'family' is made of virtues and who has no fear.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet, e.g. अथ + अभ्युदये = अथाभ्युदये.
The splitting of a sandhi form back into its separate words, e.g. कस्माद्भयम् = कस्मात् + भयम्.
The conjugation of a verb-root through persons and numbers, e.g. √त्यज्: त्यजति / त्यजतः / त्यजन्ति.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 3)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate the following verse into simple English:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
questions.answer: O noble one, enthusiasm (उत्साह) is mighty; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For a person full of enthusiasm, nothing at all in the world is hard to attain (दुर्लभ). It teaches that zeal and courage are the greatest power for achieving any goal.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: धैर्यम्, आपद्, क्षमा, विघ्नः, उत्साहः.
questions.answer: धैर्यम् = courage/steadiness; आपद् = calamity/adversity; क्षमा = patience/forgiveness; विघ्नः = obstacle; उत्साहः = enthusiasm/zeal.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the moral of 'प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति'.
questions.answer: It means the noble (उत्तमजन) never abandon a task they have begun. The moral is that we must persevere — keep courage and keep trying despite obstacles, and never give up.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) अथाभ्युदये (b) कस्माद्भयम्.
questions.answer: (a) अथाभ्युदये = अथ + अभ्युदये (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) कस्माद्भयम् = कस्मात् + भयम् (त् → द् before भ, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each word: आपदि, विघ्नैः, महात्मनाम्.
questions.answer: आपदि = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in adversity'. विघ्नैः = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by obstacles'. महात्मनाम् = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of great souls'.
questions.explanation: Locative shows place/time, instrumental shows means, genitive shows possession.

questions.question: Explain the verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...' and describe the three types of people it mentions. How can a student follow its teaching?
questions.answer:
The verse divides people into three kinds according to how they face obstacles (विघ्न). The low (नीच) never even begin a task, out of fear of obstacles. The middling (मध्यम) begin but stop as soon as obstacles strike them. But the noble (उत्तमजन), though struck again and again by obstacles, never abandon what they have begun (न परित्यजन्ति). The verse teaches that true greatness lies in persevering to the very end.
A student can follow this teaching by not fearing hard subjects, by continuing to study even after failure, by treating each difficulty as an obstacle to overcome rather than a reason to quit, and by keeping steady daily effort with courage and enthusiasm. In short: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् — never abandon courage.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about courage and effort (धैर्य / उत्साह). Give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. धीरः आपदि न विषीदति। (The steadfast person does not lose heart in adversity.)
2. उत्साहेन कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति। (Tasks are accomplished by enthusiasm.)
3. छात्रः धैर्यं न त्यजति। (The student does not abandon courage.)
Together they say: we should keep courage in trouble, work with enthusiasm, and never give up.
questions.explanation: Simple sentences using chapter vocabulary and √त्यज्.

questions.question: Translate 'आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा' and state its lesson.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Courage in adversity, and patience (forgiveness) in prosperity.' Lesson: a great person keeps a steady, appropriate virtue in every situation — courage when in trouble, humility and patience when successful.

questions.question: What does the title 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' mean, and from which धातु is 'त्याज्यम्' formed?
questions.answer: 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' means 'courage must never be abandoned'. 'त्याज्यम्' is a gerundive (कृत्य) meaning 'that which is to be given up', formed from the धातु √त्यज् ('to abandon').

questions.question: Explain how the verse 'धैर्यं यस्य पिता...' shows that a virtuous person is fearless.
questions.answer: The verse pictures a person whose 'family' is made of virtues — courage as father, patience as mother, peace as wife, truth as son, compassion as sister, self-control as brother — and whose food is the nectar of knowledge. Because such a person is surrounded and supported by these good qualities, the poet asks 'कस्माद्भयं योगिनः' — from what could he possibly have fear? A life built on virtues is content and fearless.
questions.explanation: Virtues as family lead to fearlessness.

What does the chapter title 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' mean, and what is its central teaching?
questions.answer: It means 'courage (धैर्य) should never be abandoned (न त्याज्यम्)'. Its central teaching is that one must keep steadiness and courage of mind even in adversity, and never give up.

questions.question: Explain the words धीर and कातर, and say which one this chapter asks us to be.
questions.answer: धीर means a firm, steadfast, courageous person; कातर means a coward who loses heart in difficulty. The chapter asks us to be धीर — to hold on to धैर्य and not become कातर.

questions.question: Write the first line of the perseverance verse (प्रारभ्यते...) in Devanagari.
According to 'आपदि धैर्यम्...', name any four situations and the virtue proper to each.
questions.answer: In adversity (आपद्) — courage (धैर्य); in prosperity (अभ्युदय) — patience (क्षमा); in an assembly (सदस्) — eloquence (वाक्पटुता); in battle (युध्) — valour (विक्रम).
questions.explanation: Four situation-virtue pairs from the verse.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'उत्साहो बलवान्' in one sentence.
questions.answer: It means 'enthusiasm (उत्साह) is powerful/mighty' — zeal and courage are a great source of strength.

questions.question: Explain the message of the verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...'.
questions.answer: The verse describes three kinds of people: the low (नीच) never begin a task, for fear of obstacles; the middling (मध्यम) begin but stop when obstacles strike; but the noble (उत्तमजन), though struck again and again by obstacles (विघ्न), never abandon what they have begun. The message: true greatness lies in persevering to the end.
questions.explanation: Three types; perseverance of the noble.

questions.question: What does the verse 'धैर्यं यस्य पिता...' say about fear, and why?
questions.answer: It says such a person (yogī) has nothing to fear (कस्माद्भयम्), because he is surrounded by a 'family' of virtues — courage as father, patience as mother, peace as wife, truth as son, compassion as sister, self-control as brother. Armed with these, he is fearless.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: धैर्यम्, आपद्, विघ्नः.
questions.answer: धैर्यम् = courage/steadiness; आपद् = calamity/adversity; विघ्नः = obstacle/hindrance.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: उत्साहः, बलम्, दुर्लभम्.
questions.answer: उत्साहः = enthusiasm/zeal; बलम् = strength; दुर्लभम् = hard to attain.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: क्षमा, विक्रमः, वाक्पटुता.
questions.answer: क्षमा = patience/forgiveness; विक्रमः = valour/prowess; वाक्पटुता = eloquence/skill in speech.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: जननी, सूनुः, भगिनी.
questions.answer: जननी = mother; सूनुः = son; भगिनी = sister.

questions.question: State and briefly explain the moral of 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...'.
questions.answer: The moral is that we must persevere. Obstacles (विघ्न) test everyone, but success belongs to those who do not give up. Cowards never even start; weak people quit midway; only the courageous, who keep trying despite repeated failures, achieve their goal. So we should hold on to धैर्य and never abandon a good task.

questions.question: How can a student apply the lesson 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' when they fail a test?
questions.answer: Instead of losing heart or giving up studies, the student should stay calm (धैर्य), find out the mistakes, work harder with fresh enthusiasm (उत्साह), and try again. Failure is only an obstacle (विघ्न) to overcome, not a reason to quit.

questions.question: 'When a big problem suddenly arises, some people panic.' Using the verses, explain what one should do instead.
questions.answer: The verse 'आपदि धैर्यम्' teaches that in calamity one should keep courage, not panic. A steady, courageous mind can think clearly and find a solution, while fear only makes things worse. As 'उत्साहो बलवान्' adds, zeal and courage make even hard things attainable. So one should stay calm, keep courage, and act with determination.
questions.explanation: Applies धैर्य and उत्साह to a crisis.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा'.
questions.answer: 'Courage in adversity, and patience/forgiveness in prosperity' — आपदि (in calamity) धैर्यम् (courage), अभ्युदये (in prosperity) क्षमा (patience).

questions.question: Translate the verse 'उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्, सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्'.
questions.answer: 'O noble one, enthusiasm is mighty; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For a person full of enthusiasm, nothing at all in the world is hard to attain.' It teaches that zeal and courage are the greatest power for achieving any goal.

questions.question: Translate 'प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति' and name its moral in one phrase.
questions.answer: 'The noble do not abandon what they have begun (प्रारब्ध).' Moral in one phrase: never give up / perseverance wins.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) अथाभ्युदये (b) ज्ञानामृतम्.
questions.answer: (a) अथाभ्युदये = अथ + अभ्युदये (अ + अ = आ). (b) ज्ञानामृतम् = ज्ञान + अमृतम् (अ + अ = आ).

questions.question: Join by sandhi and name the type: (a) कस्मात् + भयम् (b) अस्ति + उत्साहात्.
questions.answer: (a) कस्मात् + भयम् = कस्माद्भयम् (त् → द्, व्यञ्जन/जश्त्व-सन्धि). (b) अस्ति + उत्साहात् = अस्त्युत्साहात् (इ + उ → य्, यण्-सन्धि).

questions.question: Give the विभक्ति (case) and role of: (a) विघ्नैः (b) महात्मनाम्.
questions.answer: (a) विघ्नैः = तृतीया (instrumental) plural — 'by obstacles'. (b) महात्मनाम् = षष्ठी (genitive) plural — 'of great souls'.

questions.question: Write the धातुरूप of √त्यज् (लट्, present, परस्मैपद) in the प्रथमपुरुष (all three numbers).
questions.answer: प्रथमपुरुष: एकवचन त्यजति, द्विवचन त्यजतः, बहुवचन त्यजन्ति.

questions.question: Which विभक्ति do the endings '-एषु' and '-नाम्' usually mark? Give the English sense of each.
questions.answer: '-एषु' marks सप्तमी (locative) plural, meaning 'in/among' (e.g. लोकेषु = in the worlds). '-नाम्' marks षष्ठी (genitive) plural, meaning 'of' (e.g. महात्मनाम् = of great souls).

questions.question: What is meant by 'धैर्य', and why does the chapter 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' say it must never be abandoned? Explain with reference to the theme.
questions.answer:
धैर्य means firmness, patience and courage of mind — the quality of staying calm and steady instead of panicking or giving up. The chapter title 'त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्' literally means 'courage should not be abandoned', built from the gerundive त्याज्यम् (to be given up) of √त्यज् and the negative न.
The chapter says धैर्य must never be abandoned because life is full of difficulties (आपद्) and obstacles (विघ्न). A person who loses courage becomes helpless and cannot solve any problem, while a courageous, steady mind can think clearly and keep working towards the goal. Difficulties come and go, but the one who holds on to धैर्य and keeps trying finally succeeds. That is why steadiness of mind, even in adversity, is treasured as one of the highest virtues.
questions.explanation: Definition of धैर्य + why it must be kept.

questions.question: Write any TWO verses from this lesson in Devanagari and state the theme of each.
questions.answer:
1. प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः। विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति॥ — Theme: perseverance; the noble never give up despite obstacles.
2. उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥ — Theme: enthusiasm and courage are the greatest strength; for the zealous nothing is unattainable.

questions.question: Take the verse 'आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः, यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम्'. Give the word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: आपदि = in adversity; धैर्यम् = courage; अभ्युदये = in prosperity; क्षमा = patience/forgiveness; सदसि = in the assembly; वाक्पटुता = eloquence; युधि = in battle; विक्रमः = valour; यशसि = in fame; अभिरुचिः = liking/eagerness; व्यसनम् = deep devotion (here, to learning); श्रुतौ = in scripture/learning; प्रकृतिसिद्धम् = natural/inborn; महात्मनाम् = of great souls.
Explanation: The verse lists the virtues great souls show in different situations — courage in adversity, patience in prosperity, eloquence in an assembly, valour in battle, love of good fame, and deep devotion to learning. It then says these qualities are प्रकृतिसिद्ध, i.e. naturally present, in great souls. The verse teaches that a truly great person shows the right virtue at the right time, and that keeping courage in trouble (आपदि धैर्यम्) is the very first of these.

questions.question: Explain, with meanings, how the verse 'धैर्यं यस्य पिता...' pictures virtues as members of a family.
questions.answer: The verse imagines a virtuous person (yogī) as living in a household made entirely of good qualities: धैर्य (courage) is his father (पिता), क्षमा (patience) his mother (जननी), शान्ति (peace) his lifelong wife (गेहिनी), सत्य (truth) his son (सूनु), दया (compassion) his sister (भगिनी), and मनःसंयम (self-control) his brother (भ्राता). The bare earth (भूमितल) is his bed, the directions (दिशः) his clothing, and the nectar of knowledge (ज्ञानामृत) his food. The poet then asks: with such a family of virtues, what fear can there be for such a person (कस्माद्भयं योगिनः)? The verse teaches that a life built on good qualities is fearless and content.

questions.question: Discuss the theme of perseverance and courage in this chapter, and explain how a student can practise it in daily life.
questions.answer:
The whole chapter teaches that courage and perseverance (धैर्य) must never be abandoned. 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु...' shows that success belongs not to those who fear obstacles and never start, nor to those who quit midway, but to the noble who keep going despite repeated blows. 'आपदि धैर्यम्' teaches courage precisely in the moment of calamity, and 'उत्साहो बलवान्' declares that for the enthusiastic nothing is unattainable. 'धैर्यं यस्य पिता...' adds that a person rooted in such virtues has nothing to fear.
A student can practise this by not giving up when a subject is hard, by staying calm during exams and problems, by treating failure as an obstacle to overcome rather than a defeat, by keeping steady daily effort, and by encouraging friends who feel discouraged. In every difficulty the rule is the same — त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्, never abandon courage.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the verses of this chapter.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words. Examples from the verses:
1. अथ + अभ्युदये = अथाभ्युदये (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
2. ज्ञान + अमृतम् = ज्ञानामृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
3. अस्ति + उत्साहात् = अस्त्युत्साहात् (इ + उ → य्, यण्-सन्धि).
4. कस्मात् + भयम् = कस्माद्भयम् (त् → द् before भ, व्यञ्जन/जश्त्व-सन्धि).
Being able both to join (सन्धि) and to split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) these forms is essential for reading Sanskrit verses correctly.

questions.question: Using words from the verses, explain any four विभक्ति (cases) with one example each, and give the present-tense धातुरूप of √त्यज्.
questions.answer:
Cases (with verse examples):
1. प्रथमा (nominative, subject): धैर्यम्, क्षमा — the subjects of the verse.
2. तृतीया (instrumental, 'by'): विघ्नैः 'by obstacles', विघ्नभयेन 'by fear of obstacles'.
3. षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): महात्मनाम् 'of great souls', सोत्साहस्य 'of the enthusiastic one'.
4. सप्तमी (locative, 'in'): आपदि 'in adversity', अभ्युदये 'in prosperity', लोकेषु 'in the worlds'.
धातुरूप of √त्यज् (लट्, present, परस्मैपद): प्रथमपुरुष — त्यजति, त्यजतः, त्यजन्ति; मध्यमपुरुष — त्यजसि, त्यजथः, त्यजथ; उत्तमपुरुष — त्यजामि, त्यजावः, त्यजामः.
questions.explanation: Four cases with examples + full present conjugation.

questions.question: Translate the verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः, विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति' into English and explain its moral.
questions.answer:
Translation: 'Out of fear of obstacles, the low (नीच) never even begin a task. The middling (मध्यम), having begun, stop when obstacles strike them. But the noble (उत्तमजन), though struck again and again by obstacles, never abandon what they have begun.'
Explanation of the moral: The verse compares three kinds of people by how they face obstacles (विघ्न). Cowards do not start at all; weak people quit midway; but the truly great persevere to the very end no matter how many times they are struck down. The moral is that success belongs to those who keep courage and never give up — the essence of त्याज्यं न धैर्यम्.
questions.explanation: Full translation + moral of the perseverance verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः।
विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति॥
(a) What do the low (नीच) do? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'विघ्नैः'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'विघ्नैः'? (d) State the moral.
questions.answer: (a) The low never even begin a task, for fear of obstacles. (b) विघ्नैः = 'by obstacles'. (c) विघ्नैः is तृतीया (instrumental) plural. (d) Moral: never abandon a task; the noble persevere despite repeated obstacles.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा
सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः।
(a) What virtue is shown in adversity? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'क्षमा'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'धैर्यमथाभ्युदये'. (d) What does the verse teach overall?
questions.answer: (a) Courage (धैर्य) is shown in adversity. (b) क्षमा = patience/forgiveness. (c) धैर्यमथाभ्युदये = धैर्यम् + अथ + अभ्युदये. (d) It teaches that great souls show the right virtue in every situation — courage in trouble, patience in success, eloquence in assembly, valour in battle.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
(a) What is said to be mighty? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दुर्लभम्'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'लोकेषु'? (d) What is the message?
questions.answer: (a) Enthusiasm (उत्साह) is said to be mighty/powerful. (b) दुर्लभम् = hard to attain. (c) लोकेषु is सप्तमी (locative) plural — 'in the worlds'. (d) Message: for a person full of enthusiasm and courage, nothing in the world is unattainable.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
धैर्यं यस्य पिता क्षमा च जननी शान्तिः चिरं गेहिनी
सत्यं सूनुरयं दया च भगिनी भ्राता मनःसंयमः।
(a) Who is the 'father'? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'जननी'. (c) Which virtue is the 'brother'? (d) What is the lesson of the verse?
questions.answer: (a) Courage (धैर्य) is the father. (b) जननी = mother. (c) Self-control (मनःसंयम) is the brother. (d) Lesson: a person whose life is built on virtues — courage, patience, peace, truth, compassion, self-control — is fearless and content.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
धैर्यं यस्य पिता ... शय्या भूमितलं दिशोऽपि वसनं ज्ञानामृतं भोजनं
एते यस्य कुटुम्बिनो वद सखे कस्माद्भयं योगिनः॥
(a) What is the yogī's food? (b) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'ज्ञानामृतम्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'कस्माद्भयम्'. (d) Why has the yogī nothing to fear?
questions.answer: (a) The yogī's food is the nectar of knowledge (ज्ञानामृत). (b) ज्ञानामृतम् = ज्ञान + अमृतम्. (c) कस्माद्भयम् = कस्मात् + भयम्. (d) Because he is surrounded by a 'family' of virtues (courage, patience, peace, truth, compassion, self-control), he has nothing to fear.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः।
विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति॥
(a) What do the 'मध्यम' (middling) people do? (b) What do the 'उत्तम' (noble) do? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'परित्यजन्ति'. (d) Which type should we try to be, and why?
questions.answer: (a) The middling begin a task but stop when obstacles strike. (b) The noble, though struck again and again by obstacles, never abandon what they have begun. (c) परित्यजन्ति = '(they) abandon/give up'. (d) We should be the उत्तम (noble) type, because only steady perseverance leads to success.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा ... यशसि चाभिरुचिर्व्यसनं श्रुतौ
प्रकृतिसिद्धमिदं हि महात्मनाम्॥
(a) In which विभक्ति are 'आपदि' and 'श्रुतौ'? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'महात्मनाम्'? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'प्रकृतिसिद्धम्'. (d) Whose qualities are these said to be?
questions.answer: (a) आपदि and श्रुतौ are सप्तमी (locative) — 'in adversity', 'in learning'. (b) महात्मनाम् is षष्ठी (genitive) plural — 'of great souls'. (c) प्रकृतिसिद्धम् = natural/inborn. (d) These qualities are said to be the natural, inborn qualities of great souls (महात्मन्).

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
(a) Translate 'नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'बलम्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नास्ति'. (d) What is the central theme?
questions.answer: (a) 'There is no strength greater than enthusiasm.' (b) बलम् = strength. (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति. (d) Central theme: enthusiasm and courage (उत्साह) are the greatest power for achieving any goal.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
A student, after failing twice, feels like giving up studies. Recall the verses of this chapter.
(a) Which verse best advises this student? (b) What are the three types of people in that verse? (c) What should the student decide? (d) State the chapter's one-line message.
questions.answer: (a) The verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...' best advises the student. (b) The three types are: नीच (never begin), मध्यम (begin but quit at obstacles), and उत्तम (never abandon despite obstacles). (c) The student should decide to be उत्तम — to keep trying and not give up. (d) One-line message: त्याज्यं न धैर्यम् — never abandon courage.
questions.explanation: Applies perseverance to a real situation.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
आपदि धैर्यमथाभ्युदये क्षमा
सदसि वाक्पटुता युधि विक्रमः।
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'वाक्पटुता'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'विक्रमः'. (c) In which situation should one show विक्रम? (d) What single idea links all the qualities in this verse?
questions.answer: (a) वाक्पटुता = eloquence/skill in speech. (b) विक्रमः = valour/prowess. (c) One should show विक्रम (valour) in battle (युधि). (d) The single idea: a great soul shows the right, appropriate virtue in each situation of life.
